**RE: Appeal of the denial dated August 7, 2026 — Reference number POC-99CC30886D-55239**

- **Member:** Morgan Carter
- **Member ID:** W450765041
- **Plan / Product:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care, Commercial/ACA (Maine)
- **Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
- **Governing policy:** *2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review — Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766)*, https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), which Harvard Pilgrim issued on August 7, 2026 under reference number POC-99CC30886D-55239. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in the file address the plan's own published criteria point by point. Below I match each criterion I was given to the specific records.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Imaging that matches the clinical findings.** The policy requires:

> "Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings"

My imaging is dated June 23, 2026 and consists of an MRI of the lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs. They show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. My physical exam documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. The imaging and the exam findings describe the same problem at the same level.

**2. A qualifying clinical condition — spondylolisthesis.** The policy lists, among the conditions it recognizes:

> "Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia)"

My imaging documents grade I **degenerative spondylolisthesis** at L4-L5 — one of the exact conditions named in that sentence.

**3. A qualifying clinical condition — segmental instability.** The policy also lists:

> "Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability, and surgically induced segmental instability"

Flexion-extension radiographs were obtained specifically to measure motion, and they document 5 mm of translation at L4-L5 in the setting of degenerative spondylolisthesis. The excerpt of the policy I have does not state a millimeter threshold for "excessive motion," and I am not assuming one. If the plan applied a numeric threshold, I ask that it tell me what that threshold is and where it appears in the guideline.

**4. Failure of conservative treatment.** The policy requires:

> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"

I completed supervised physical therapy from April 15, 2026 to June 24, 2026 — 10 weeks and 24 completed visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That period is longer than six weeks and falls within the six months before the request.

**5. What counts as "failure."** The policy defines it this way:

> "NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ■ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR ■ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR ■ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment"

Only one of those three needs to be met. My records show the first two. I have had 12 months of **progressive** pain in my lower back and legs that is not relieved by rest. I took NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on April 10, 2026 gave me only two weeks of partial relief. I finished the full course of therapy — 24 of 24 visits — and I still cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop.

I would add that the policy states:

> "Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

None of that applies to me. I did not miss or abandon treatment; I completed it, and it did not work.

**6. Multimodality treatment with active and inactive components.** The policy requires:

> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

My active component was supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. My inactive components were six months of NSAIDs and the lumbar corticosteroid injection on April 10, 2026. Both types of treatment were directed at my lumbar spine — the region being operated on.

**7. Symptom duration and daily function.** One of the policy's criteria reads:

> "Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months"

My symptoms have lasted 12 months, twice the six months this criterion describes, and they clearly impair my daily activities — I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before I have to sit down. I want to be straightforward with the reviewer: my exam also documents diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, so if the plan reads this particular criterion as applying only to patients without a sensory deficit, then my case is better addressed under the spondylolisthesis and segmental instability criteria quoted above, which my imaging meets directly.

**8. A clear surgical plan.** The policy requires:

> "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery."

The request submitted on my behalf was for lumbar fusion, CPT 22612, by Dr. Okafor of orthopedic surgery, at the L4-L5 level where my imaging shows the spondylolisthesis, the 5 mm of translation, and the severe central stenosis. If the plan believes the surgical plan in the file is not specific enough, I ask that it say exactly which element it found missing, so my surgeon's office can send that one document rather than resubmit the whole packet.

## What I am asking the plan to clarify

The denial did not tell me which criterion my documentation failed to satisfy — it said only that the documentation was incomplete. The excerpts of the guideline I have also include criteria that do not appear to apply to me (revision surgery for pseudoarthrosis or repeat disc herniation, and fusion for spinal tumor, cancer, or infection), and the guideline lists further clinical conditions that are not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. So that I can respond specifically, I ask the plan to identify:

1. the exact criterion or criteria from the *2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review — Musculoskeletal Surgery (Lumbar Spine Surgery, CG 1766)* that it applied to my request; and
2. the specific document or finding it considered missing from the submitted packet.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to overturn the August 7, 2026 denial and approve CPT 22612, or, if any single document is still needed, to tell me what it is so it can be provided promptly. I understand this appeal must be received by **February 3, 2027**, and I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I can also be reached through Member Services at **1-888-333-4742**.

I am also willing to provide any of the following on request: the physical therapy discharge note covering April 15 – June 24, 2026; the June 23, 2026 MRI and flexion-extension radiograph reports; my medication and injection records; and Dr. Okafor's operative plan and office notes.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my records. I would like the chance to get back to standing and walking without stopping every ten minutes, and my surgeon has documented that this surgery is what I need.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Carter**
